comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Option 2 built - a surface belongs to its pane and is owned by the window, lent to whichever region shows it. Switching a tab away keeps its bridges running; switching back starts none. New Sources/MusterMac/PaneSurfaces.swift, with RegionView borrowing rather than owning.

The user chose this over the other three. Worth recording why the fourth is still open: one multiplexed frame stream per machine is the only option that removes the 400ms rather than moving it, and it is a bridge-protocol change - raised as its own card.

Not measured, and both halves of the card's 'Validating a fix' need a machine this one is not. ./dev --perf is the tier that judges holding fifteen surfaces where three were held, and it refuses a loaded machine; this one is hosting live agent sessions. The 440ms needs a devenv, and ./dev --ssh recreates the container. Both worth running before this is trusted.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Switching to a devenv tab leaves the pane blank for about half a second before its text appears. Local panes appear immediately. Reported while driving a laptop and a devenv side by side, and measurable in the run log.

## Where the time goes

Time from `bridge.start` to `bridge.frame.first`, taken from one session's log:

    local panes    29ms, 59ms
    devenv panes   444-561ms, median ~490ms, 17 samples

The frame itself is not the cost. Those devenv frames ranged from 149KB to 420KB, and the largest took 561ms against 465ms for the smallest - a 2.8x increase in bytes for 20% more time. There is a fixed cost of roughly 440ms and a small per-byte one.

The fixed cost is the far machine opening a session. Timed against the ssh master Muster already holds open:

    ssh -S <master> -O check <host>          20ms    (local client, no remote work)
    ssh -S <master> <host> 'exec /bin/true'  410ms   (a channel and a process, no shell)
    ssh -S <master> <host> 'herdr --version' 415ms   (so herdr's own startup is ~5ms)
    ping <host>                              2.7ms   round trip

So it is not the network, not herdr, and not the local ssh client. It is the box taking ~400ms to spawn a session for a new channel - a shared devenv, load average 19-29, up ten days. Every bridge Muster starts pays it.

## Why it is paid on every switch

Muster starts a bridge per surface, and a surface exists for the pane a region is currently showing. Switch to a devenv tab and its pane gets a new surface, a new `muster-bridge`, a new `ssh` exec, and therefore a fresh 400ms session setup. The same session's log holds seventeen `bridge.start` records for three devenv panes: the cost is paid per switch, not per pane.

The same 400ms is paid for every remote pane at launch, and again on every relaunch. It is also what makes `a_2Ht74jTXV` expensive rather than merely wrong - a duplicated surface pays it twice.

## Four ways out, in increasing order of how much they change

- **Cache the last screen and paint it immediately**, then reconcile when frames arrive. This is what was asked for, and it makes the switch feel instant. The pane shows a screen that is up to a switch old, which for an agent mid-turn is a lie the size of the delay it replaces - though "stale for 400ms" reads better than "blank for 400ms".
- **Keep the bridge alive for off-screen panes.** The cost moves from per-switch to once per pane, and switching becomes free. The price is one ssh channel, one `muster-bridge` and one herdr client per remote pane, held for as long as the pane exists - fifteen agents means fifteen of each.
- **Pre-warm the likely next pane** - the tab a chord would reach, the row the pointer is over. Cheaper than holding everything, and only ever a guess.
- **One frame stream per machine instead of one per pane.** Muster already reuses a single ssh master; what remains is one exec per pane. A single long-lived client on the far side, multiplexing every pane's frames over one channel, pays the 400ms once per machine and nothing per switch. This is the largest change - the bridge protocol is per-pane today - and the only one that removes the cost rather than moving it.

## Reproducing it

1. Attach a devenv with at least one pane and switch away from and back to its tab.
2. Read the latency out of the run log rather than by feel:

       L=$(ls -t ~/Library/Logs/muster/*.jsonl | grep -v latest | head -1)
       rg '"event":"(bridge.start|bridge.frame.first)"' "$L"

   Pair each `bridge.start` with the `bridge.frame.first` that follows it and subtract `mono_ns`.
3. Separate the far machine's session setup from everything else with the three `ssh -S` timings above, against the master in `$TMPDIR/muster-<app pid>-<daemon>.ctl`.

A fast devenv will hide this. The number that matters is what `ssh -S <master> <host> 'exec /bin/true'` costs on the machine in question; anything much above a round trip lands on every pane switch.

## Validating a fix

- Time from `bridge.start` (or whatever replaces it) to first paint on a remote pane is within a few times the local figure, not ten.
- Switching to a devenv tab and back does not start a new remote session each time - watch `bridge.start` counts, or `pgrep -f 'muster-bridge.*via-ssh'`.
- Whatever is held open scales with panes rather than with switches, and is released when a pane closes.
title: 🐢 Switching to a devenv pane waits half a second for a new ssh session
